dedupe_keys.name: meshscope ems weekly panel of difficult to place ambulance transport cases for 52 japanese fire departments 2020 2026

description: This panel counts, week by week, how often ambulance crews in Japan's major cities struggled to find a hospital that would accept their patient, a widely used signal of strain on emergency care. The producer is Kunihisa Ohno of Jinen Co., Ltd. in Kyoto, who compiled the weekly publications of Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency on cases of difficulty in securing hospital acceptance. A case counts when the crew made four or more hospital inquiries and spent 30 minutes or more on scene. Coverage is the 52 fire departments in the national survey, from April 2020 through the COVID-19 period and into the continuing series to 2026. Files give the weekly counts by department, a COVID-related subset, department covariates, national totals used to check the extraction, and the processing code with tests; a companion crosswalk allocates departments to Japan's 330 secondary medical areas. The data are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, based on government data published under terms compatible with it. Caveats: counts only, without total transports as a denominator in the main panel, and department coverage is fixed to the survey. Simulation uses: measuring how epidemics and heat waves push emergency systems into hospital access failure, and validating models of ambulance-hospital interaction. Related records: the AKTIN length of stay data (data-aktin-emergency-department-length-of-stay) track emergency department strain in Germany.
